originalTitle: Here's the inflation breakdown for July 2026 — in one chart
summary: Costs remain elevated for consumers, however inflation is showing some signs of easing, economists say.
content:
Consumer prices rose in July — a reversal of the pullback in June — but showed inflation broadly moderating, even as energy remained sharply higher than a year ago.

The consumer price index , an inflation barometer, was up 3.4% from 12 months earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Wednesday.

That's down slightly from 3.5% in June, which marked the first decline in the annual inflation rate since January, before the war between the U.S. and Iran erupted Feb. 28.

"I thought it was a very benign report, right down the strike zone," said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's. Inflation is "still high but moving in the right direction," he said, "assuming the war in Iran fades to the background."

Energy prices increased 14.7% for the 12 months ended in July amid doubts that the U.S. and Iran could reach a broader resolution to the conflict .

Prices for gasoline, which is refined from crude oil, and other fuels and energy products were also higher as a result. Gasoline prices were up 24.6% over the year while fuel oil rose 39.1%, according to the inflation data issued Wednesday.

Consumers paid a national average of $4.04 per gallon as of Wednesday, according to AAA — up from about $3.14 a year ago.

Airline fares also rose 25.5% over the past 12 months, according to the CPI data.

Still, the oil shock didn't put too much pressure on grocery prices, economists said, which have been a particular pain point for most U.S. households.

Food prices climbed 3% over the last year, according to the CPI data, with food at home prices up 2.7%.

"Food prices don't seem to be too bad, but there's a lot of mix in there," said Brian Bethune, an economics professor at Boston College. "Meat is way up, chicken is slightly down, egg prices have finally come back down, and now we have a problem with lettuce," he said.

Concerns about ongoing cyclospora outbreaks have dampened consumer demand for lettuce, which weighed on the index for fruits and vegetables.

Overall, the meats, poultry, fish and eggs index rose 1.9% over the 12 months ended in July, while the index for dairy fell 0.5% over the year.

The core CPI, which excludes food and energy, was up 2.5% on the year, with the indexes for new vehicles, apparel and shelter all notching modest increases.

"Affordability is still a serious problem," Zandi said, although "it's much better than it has been."

If these trends continue, "assuming energy prices don't go back up, inflation will be within spitting distance of the Fed's target," he said.

The Fed is in a 'wait-and-see mode'

The inflation rate is one of the key economic indicators the Federal Reserve uses to guide interest rate decisions.

The central bank voted last month to keep the benchmark rate in a range between 3.5%-3.75%, but policymakers signaled an increase in borrowing costs could be on the horizon .

With inflation remaining above the Fed's 2% target, this latest CPI reading leaves a September rate hike on the table, but the odds are higher for an October move, experts say.

"After more than five years of above-target inflation, policymakers want to see a clear and lasting trend before acting. Until then, this is a Fed in wait-and-see mode," Karen Manna, fixed income investment director at Federated Hermes, said in an email.
chineseTitle: 以下是 2026 年 7 月的通胀明细——在一张图表中
chineseSummary: 经济学家表示，消费者的成本仍然居高不下，但通胀却显示出一些缓解的迹象。
chineseContent:
7 月份消费者价格上涨（扭转了 6 月份的回调），但显示通胀总体放缓，尽管能源价格仍大幅高于一年前。

美国劳工统计局周三表示，作为通胀晴雨表的消费者价格指数较 12 个月前上涨 3.4%。

这比 6 月份的 3.5% 略有下降，这是自 2 月 28 日美国和伊朗战争爆发前 1 月份以来年度通胀率首次下降。

穆迪首席经济学家马克赞迪表示：“我认为这是一份非常良性的报告，正好处于打击区。”他表示，通胀“仍然很高，但正在朝着正确的方向发展”，“假设伊朗战争已经淡出人们的视线。”

由于人们怀疑美国和伊朗能否就冲突达成更广泛的解决方案，截至 7 月份的 12 个月里，能源价格上涨了 14.7%。

从原油中提炼的汽油以及其他燃料和能源产品的价格也因此上涨。根据周三发布的通胀数据，汽油价格同比上涨 24.6%，而燃油价格上涨 39.1%。

根据 AAA 的数据，截至周三，全国消费者平均支付每加仑 4.04 美元，高于一年前的约 3.14 美元。

根据 CPI 数据，过去 12 个月内，机票价格也上涨了 25.5%。

经济学家表示，石油危机并未对食品杂货价格造成太大压力，这对大多数美国家庭来说是一个特别的痛点。

根据CPI数据，去年食品价格上涨3%，其中家庭食品价格上涨2.7%。

波士顿学院经济学教授布莱恩·白求恩表示：“食品价格似乎并不算太​​糟糕，但其中有很多成分。” “肉类价格大幅上涨，鸡肉价格略有下降，鸡蛋价格终于回落，现在我们遇到了生菜问题，”他说。

阅读更多 CNBC 个人理财报道

对持续爆发的环孢子虫疫情的担忧抑制了消费者对生菜的需求，从而打压了水果和蔬菜指数。

总体而言，截至 7 月份的 12 个月中，肉类、家禽、鱼类和蛋类指数上涨 1.9%，而乳制品指数全年下跌 0.5%。

不包括食品和能源的核心CPI同比上涨2.5%，其中新车、服装和住房指数均小幅上涨。

“负担能力仍然是一个严重的问题，”赞迪说，尽管“现在比以前好多了。”

他表示，如果这些趋势持续下去，“假设能源价格不回升，通胀将接近美联储的目标”。

美联储处于“观望模式”

通货膨胀率是美联储用来指导利率决策的关键经济指标之一。

央行上个月投票决定将基准利率维持在3.5%-3.75%的范围内，但政策制定者暗示借贷成本可能即将增加。

专家表示，由于通胀仍高于美联储 2% 的目标，最新的消费者物价指数 (CPI) 数据使得 9 月加息成为可能，但 10 月加息的可能性更大。

Federated Hermes固定收益投资总监凯伦·曼纳(Karen Manna)在一封电子邮件中表示，“在通胀超过目标五年多之后，政策制定者希望在采取行动之前看到明显而持久的趋势。在此之前，美联储将处于观望模式。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
